title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
one_liner: 从已发表研究提取 102 个科学数据任务，以独立 Python 程序为统一产出，同时检查执行、任务结果、代码相似度和 API 成本。

problem.text: 语言 Agent 能否完成科学工作流中的数据处理、建模、分析和可视化任务？作者主张在讨论端到端科研自动化之前，先测量这些具体环节的完成能力。基准从 44 篇同行评审论文提取 102 个任务，覆盖四个学科。

gap.text: 只用整篇生成论文的整体评价，很难判断 Agent 是否真正具备基础的数据工作能力；抽象问答和少量代码补全也不足以代表实际科学任务。本文将实际论文中的程序任务整理成统一输入输出，并邀请领域专家检查其真实性与合理性。

method.text: 每个任务提供自然语言目标、数据目录与预览，以及可选的专家知识，要求生成可独立执行的 Python 文件。评测先检查运行与保存文件，再用任务专用脚本验证结果；图像结果由 GPT-4o 对照参考图评分。另报 CodeBERTScore 和 API 费用，并用五阶段专家 rubric 补充人工评价。

trace.text: 图 2 和表 1 的 ClinTox 任务要求读取分子数据，训练预测药物毒性与 FDA 批准状态的模型，并输出带分子 SMILES 和预测概率的 CSV。程序运行和输出路径须正确，训练结果还须达到测试集 ROC-AUC ≥ 0.77 的标准。能生成代码、能运行和达成科学任务目标在这里是不同层次。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入是任务说明、真实研究数据及可选领域知识；产出是一个独立 Python 源文件和指定预测、表格或图像。任务覆盖生物信息学、计算化学、地理信息科学，以及心理学与认知神经科学。数据、程序和评分规则经过标注者及九位领域专家的多轮验证。

results.text: 本文记录 arXiv v1 的结果，不混用后续版本：五个模型分别配合直接提示、OpenHands CodeAct 和 Self-Debug。每任务独立运行三次，主表按 SR、VER、CBS、成本的优先级选择最佳一次；Claude-3.5-Sonnet + Self-Debug 的任务成功率为无专家知识 32.4%、有专家知识 34.3%。附录 D 另报三次运行的均值和标准差，因此主表结果不能当成单次平均成功率。

contributions.text: 将来自真实研究论文的异构科学任务统一为完整程序生成问题，并提供任务专用验证。多轮专家核查、执行结果与成本联合报告，以及补充的过程 rubric，让读者能区分可运行性与实际任务完成。贡献是评测任务集和协议，不是已实现自主科研的系统。

limitations.text: 附录 A 明确限定为科学数据任务的代码生成，不覆盖文献总结、实验规划或整个研究生命周期。任务只收 Python，并为评测效率优先选择参考程序十分钟内可完成的任务；学科覆盖也受可用数据和专家限制。作者承认代码相似度与图像模型评审不完美，因此不能将得分直接推广到所有科学能力。

cost.text: v1 表 3 中，无专家知识时 Claude-3.5-Sonnet 的 Self-Debug API 成本为每任务 $0.057，OpenHands 为 $0.958；这些是论文当时设置下的成本记录。程序环境需要按依赖动态配置；参考程序十分钟内完成的筛选条件，不等同于所有 Agent 的运行时间限制或今天的 API 价格。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：作为科研 Agent 与代码 Agent benchmark 的例子，它适合说明任务来源、专家验证、执行检查和成本报告如何结合。阅读时可先看 §2.3 的指标定义、表 3 的配置差异及附录 D 的均值，再判断论文结果对应哪种运行口径。

en.one_liner: ScienceAgentBench extracts 102 scientific-data tasks from published studies and evaluates standalone Python solutions for execution, task outcomes, code similarity and API cost.

sections.problem: Can language agents carry out data processing, modeling, analysis and visualization in scientific workflows? The authors argue that these concrete abilities should be measured before making claims about end-to-end research automation. The benchmark draws 102 tasks from 44 peer-reviewed papers across four disciplines.
sections.gap: Overall judgments of generated papers make it hard to assess basic scientific-data work. Abstract questions and small code-completion exercises also miss practical requirements. The authors standardize programming tasks from real papers and ask domain experts to check authenticity and validity.
sections.method: Each task supplies a natural-language goal, data directory and preview, and optional expert knowledge. The agent writes a standalone Python file. Evaluation first checks execution and saved files, then uses task-specific scripts to verify results. GPT-4o compares images with references. CodeBERTScore, API cost and a five-stage expert rubric supplement these checks.
sections.trace: The ClinTox task in Figure 2 and Table 1 asks the agent to load molecular data, train models for drug toxicity and FDA approval status, and save a CSV with molecular SMILES and predicted probabilities. The program and output paths must work, and test-set ROC-AUC must reach at least 0.77. Generating runnable code and meeting the scientific target are distinct checks.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs are task instructions, research data and optional domain knowledge. Outputs are a standalone Python file and required predictions, tables or images. Fields include bioinformatics, computational chemistry, geographic information science, and psychology/cognitive neuroscience. Annotators and nine domain experts validate data, programs and scoring over multiple rounds.
sections.results: This card records arXiv v1. Five models are tested with direct prompting, OpenHands CodeAct and Self-Debug. Each task has three independent runs. The main table selects the best run by priority of SR, VER, CBS and cost. Claude-3.5-Sonnet with Self-Debug achieves 32.4% task success without expert knowledge and 34.3% with it. Appendix D separately reports three-run means and standard deviations, so the main results are not average single-run success rates.
sections.contributions: The benchmark turns heterogeneous research tasks into complete-program generation problems with task-specific verification. Expert checks, execution outcomes, cost reporting and a supplementary process rubric help distinguish runnable programs from successful scientific work.
sections.limitations: Appendix A limits the benchmark to code generation for scientific-data tasks. Literature review, experimental planning and the full research lifecycle are outside its coverage. It uses Python and favors reference programs completing within ten minutes for evaluation efficiency. Data access and expert availability constrain fields. Code similarity and image judging are imperfect measures.
sections.cost: In v1 Table 3 without expert knowledge, Claude-3.5-Sonnet costs $0.057 per task with Self-Debug and $0.958 with OpenHands in API usage. Environments need dependencies configured dynamically. The ten-minute reference-program screening criterion is separate from agent runtime limits and reported prices are specific to the experiments.
sections.relevance: Library analysis. The work illustrates how research-derived agent tasks combine expert validation, execution checks and cost reporting. Section 2.3, Table 3 and Appendix D clarify metric definitions, configuration differences and the distinction between selected-best and average results.
